requirements.requirement: Run a three-member MariaDB Galera cluster on node1, node2, node3 holding application data
requirements.summary: node1 bootstrapped via galera_new_cluster reaching wsrep_cluster_size=1/Primary; node2 and node3 joined via SST, directly observed reaching cluster_size=2 then 3 with wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced. An appdata.orders table with sample rows was created on node1 and directly queried and confirmed present with identical rows on node2 and node3.

requirements.requirement: Add node4 as a fourth member that carries the data that already exists
requirements.summary: node4 was configured with a 4-node gcomm address, started, and directly observed reaching wsrep_cluster_size=4, Synced, Primary via cmd-15ba3b24e0964368. A subsequent SELECT on node4 (cmd-5d7cbd20da4548ce) directly shows the pre-existing widget/gadget/gizmo rows present on node4 prior to any write, confirming the dataset was transferred via SST.

requirements.requirement: node4 accepts writes like the other members
requirements.summary: An INSERT executed directly on node4 (cmd-5d7cbd20da4548ce) succeeded and the new row ('node4-write-test') was directly observed on node1 in a subsequent query (cmd-85840a1515734193), confirming node4 both accepts writes and replicates them to the original members.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task are directly and coherently supported by captured command output: a healthy 3-node Galera cluster was bootstrapped and loaded with application data, node4 was added and directly shown to hold the same rows after SST, and a write executed on node4 was directly observed to replicate back to node1. The mandated provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was also completed for all four nodes with matching pre-restart baselines, restart acknowledgements, distinct post-restart boot IDs (cross-checked against the fixed after-prepare/after-executor global snapshots), and confirmed cluster/data recovery each time, with quorum preserved throughout.
limitations: The provider-wide restart protocol is supplemental to this task's contract (which does not itself require restart/recovery); it was executed with strong, consistent evidence but is not scored as a material task outcome here.
SSH private/public key material distributed via CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/PUBKEY for one-time credential propagation was left in place on all four nodes rather than being cleaned up after use.

Package-manager consistency checks (package-health) timed out on every node in both the before-prepare and after-executor snapshots, so no direct evidence of RPM database integrity is available despite several interrupted/retried yum operations.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map clearly to legitimate prerequisites (repo/GPG-key fixes after initial failures, EPEL install for the pv dependency, firewall port opening, galera.cnf writes) or to the mandated restart-verification protocol. Repeated failed attempts (proxy timeouts writing mariadb.repo cmd-d8289730c0ce4e27/cmd-6f6a367dbeb24426; missing-dependency install cmd-b90b0551fa1b49b7 family; GPG 404 cmd-0fca0d76b20c4420 family) were genuine discovery/troubleshooting toward the same goal and were corrected in follow-up commands, not abandoned. The generated root password was copied through /home/antrieb/.mariadb_root_pass on all four nodes and then explicitly deleted afterward (cmd-c9cbd6dbdf5c407d, cmd-a766d35b904946dc, cmd-863ab6d244a44a2f, cmd-3adcd276e2e94b21), so that transient credential file did not persist. However, the CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY material written to node1's ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 (cmd-24d1bd6d9bb94797) and the corresponding CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY appended to authorized_keys on node2/node3/node4 (cmd-781307cd059f46a8, cmd-e6a09c8789fc4c6b, cmd-af682dbe16164b6e) were never removed after the one-time credential distribution task was complete, leaving standing SSH trust and a private key on disk as residue. Install logs and a yum transaction-save file were also left in /tmp on all nodes (visible in the after-executor snapshot), which is low-risk residue typical of package installs.
